title: A part on an open work order can be deactivated, Cycle count blocks bulk
custom_preconds:
1. You are on the Parts -> Inventory page on the build under test, with permission to view inventory parts.
  2. You hold the "Part Library & Inventory - Delete" permission (needed to change status/tracking).
  3. A part that is currently on an open work order.
custom_steps:
1. Deactivate that part (via bulk mode or its edit dialog) and confirm.
  2. Check the open work order still carries the part and its history.
  3. Confirm the status change is recorded in the part's own history.
  4. Start Cycle count and try to reach the bulk-status entry in the actions menu.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • If a part being set inactive sits on an open work order the change still goes through, the part stays on that work order, and its work order and invoice history is not changed (only the status change is recorded in the part's own history, per Story 10).
  • Cycle count and bulk status cannot both be on: while Cycle count runs the actions menu is replaced by the count controls, so the bulk-status entry cannot be reached until the count is saved or discarded.

Source - where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10647; "Parts Lifecycle Update" PRD (Confluence 829227015, IN REVIEW 2026-09-09), Story 2 (Deactivate parts); design canvas Vz6rprcWyP16tYxzM1kdeE; read 30 Sep 2026. Source-verified 30 September 2026 against an IN-REVIEW spec; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S2-E1: “If a part being set inactive sits on an open work order, the change still goes through.”
  • S2-E2: “That part stays on the open work order.”
  • S2-E3: “The part's work order and invoice history is not changed. The status change itself is recorded in the part's own history, per Story 10.”
  • S2-E4: “Cycle count and bulk status cannot both be on. While Cycle count is running the actions menu is replaced by the count controls, so there is no way to reach the bulk status entry until the count is saved or discarded.”
